camera.definition: A device used to record moving pictures and sound.

tripod.definition: A three-legged stand that keeps a camera steady.

boom-microphone.definition: A microphone on a long pole held above the people being recorded.

spotlight.definition: A strong focused light that shines on one part of a stage.

softbox-light.definition: A light with a cover that creates soft, even illumination.

teleprompter.definition: A screen that shows a presenter the words to say.

green-screen.definition: A green background used to add different images during editing.

dolly.definition: A wheeled platform used to move a camera smoothly.

jib-crane.definition: A movable arm that carries a camera for high or sweeping shots.

monitor-wall.definition: A group of screens showing several video feeds at once.

anchor-desk.definition: The desk where a news presenter sits during a broadcast.

background-set.definition: The scenery placed behind people in a television program or recorded scene.

stage.definition: An area where performers or presenters appear on camera.

platform.definition: A raised surface used for equipment, sets, or performances.

curtain.definition: A long piece of hanging fabric drawn across a window at night.

props.definition: Objects used by performers or placed in a scene.

clock.definition: A round face with moving hands that shows the time.

logo.definition: A design that identifies a company, channel, or program.

backdrop.definition: A background placed behind a subject or scene.

floor-marking.definition: A visible mark showing where a person or object should stand.

director.definition: The person who controls how a television production is made.

producer.definition: The person who organises the people, money, and work for a program.

camera-operator.definition: A person who controls a camera during filming or broadcasting.

sound-engineer.definition: A person who records, mixes, and improves the program’s sound.

lighting-technician.definition: A person who sets up and controls lights for a production.

makeup-artist.definition: A person who applies makeup for performers or presenters before filming begins.

set-designer.definition: A person who plans and creates the scenery for a production.

script-writer.definition: A person who writes the words and action for a program.

editor.definition: A person who selects and arranges recorded material.

stage-manager.definition: A person who coordinates people and equipment backstage during a production.

live-broadcast.definition: A program transmitted while the event is happening in real time.

recording.definition: A stored copy of video or sound that can be played again later.

satellite-dish.definition: A curved antenna that receives television signals from a satellite in space.

antenna.definition: A device that sends or receives radio and television signals.

transmitter.definition: Equipment that sends a radio, television, or communication signal over a distance.

signal.definition: An electrical or radio message that carries information.

channel.definition: A television service or a numbered path for a signal.

frequency.definition: The number of times a radio wave repeats each second.

broadcast-tower.definition: A tall structure that sends radio or television signals across a wide area.

control-room.definition: A room where staff monitor and control a television broadcast.

microphone.definition: A device that changes sound into an electrical recording or signal.

headphones.definition: Two padded cups joined by a band, worn over the ears.

mixer.definition: Equipment used to combine and control different sound sources.

amplifier.definition: A device that makes an audio signal stronger.

speaker.definition: A box that plays sound out loud into the room.

sound-board.definition: A panel used to adjust the volume and quality of sounds.

clip-on-mic.definition: A small microphone attached to a person’s clothing for clear speech.

pop-filter.definition: A screen that reduces popping sounds when someone speaks into a microphone.

audio-cable.definition: A cable that carries sound from one device to another.

equalizer.definition: A control that adjusts different ranges of sound frequencies.

editing-suite.definition: A room or computer system used to edit recorded media.

timeline.definition: A display showing the order and length of clips in an edit.

cut.definition: To remove part of a recording or change to another shot.

transition.definition: A change from one video shot or scene to another.

special-effect.definition: An image or sound created to produce an unusual result.

color-grading.definition: Adjusting video colours to create a consistent visual style across different shots.

subtitle.definition: Text on screen showing spoken words or translations.

voiceover.definition: Spoken words recorded to accompany images without showing the speaker.

render.definition: To process a project into a finished video or audio file.

export.definition: To save a finished project in a chosen file format.

monitor.definition: A screen that displays images or information from equipment.

boom-mic.definition: A microphone mounted on a pole to record sound from above.

clapperboard.definition: A board snapped before filming to identify and synchronise a shot.

anchor.definition: A presenter who leads a television news program.

reporter.definition: A journalist who gathers information and presents news.

cameraman.definition: A person who operates a camera during filming.

technician.definition: A person who maintains and operates technical equipment during a production.

live.definition: Broadcast or performed at the same time as it happens.

commercial.definition: A short advertisement shown between television programs to promote a product or service.

interview.definition: A conversation in which one person asks another questions.

segment.definition: One part of a television program that focuses on a particular topic.

headline.definition: A short title that introduces the main news story.

weather-map.definition: A map showing weather conditions across an area during a news forecast.
